name: Awn
author: E. T. Carter
description: A glowing sea of wheat: many ranks of awned stalks recede from the horizon down to the foreground, each a slender curved stroke topped by a fine fuzzy bristle-fan seed-head. Invisible gust fronts sweep across as travelling waves of bow-and-spring-back, pouring iridescent palette light into the heads and bristles in proportion to flex, so a luminous ripple runs through the field under a faint dusk horizon.

params.label: Gust rate
params.effect: How often gust fronts arrive to ripple across the sea of grass.

params.label: Bend
params.effect: How deeply stalks bow under a front and how far the spring-back overshoots.

params.label: Stalk spacing
params.effect: CSS-pixel spacing between stalks in the nearest rank, from a dense field of wheat to a sparse stand.

params.label: Head glow
params.effect: How brightly the bristle-fan seed-heads glow, from a muted field to a vivid iridescent sea.

params.label: Scatter
params.effect: Randomness of stalk placement and height — 0 is a neat regimented row, 1 a wild naturally-jittered field.

params.label: Viewable distance
params.effect: How far the field recedes — low brings the grass close and tall, high lifts the horizon so more rows stack into the distance.
